findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database volume, and any snapshots derived from it, store customer data in cleartext on disk without KMS protection.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, expanding the attack surface of a backend data store that only the application EC2 instance needs to reach.

The master username is hard-coded as 'admin' and the password is supplied via var.password, which is rendered into the Terraform state and into the EC2 user_data; no Secrets Manager / managed master password is used.

The user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user_data is readable by anyone with instance metadata access (including via SSRF from the PHP app) and is stored unencrypted in the instance description and Terraform state.

No metadata_options block is specified, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with a web application that performs user-supplied input handling, this allows an SSRF to retrieve the instance profile credentials of the highly privileged catalog_app_role.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is set, so the instance's EBS volumes—which hold the plaintext dbinfo.inc containing the database password—may be created unencrypted.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role attached to the internet-facing web server. Compromise of the PHP application yields near-total control of storage, compute and databases in the account, including a privilege-escalation path via ec2:RunInstances/iam pass-through and rds:ModifyDBInstance.
The database security group allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting unrestricted outbound traffic that facilitates data exfiltration from a compromised database host.

This security group is the only network control on a database marked publicly_accessible; its ingress rule scopes to the VPC CIDR but the group carries no description and relies entirely on separate rule resources, leaving the publicly routable endpoint dependent on a single, easily widened rule.

No parameter enforcing TLS (require_secure_transport) is set in the attached parameter group and the PHP client connects with plain mysqli_connect, so credentials and query data traverse the network unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced in parameter group
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and omits require_secure_transport = 1, so the database accepts unencrypted client connections.
The database endpoint is emitted as an unmarked Terraform output, disclosing the location of a publicly accessible database to anyone with access to state or CI logs.
